sentences.text: This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

Heard Mr. R.P.Kar, learned Senior Counsel with Mr. A.Mishra  for the petitioner, Mr. B.Bhuyan, learned counsel appearing for the  State in OPID matters, Mr. B.Pattnaik, learned counsel appearing  for one of the informants.

3. The petitioner is in custody in connection with Bhubaneswar  P.S. Case No. 09 of 2023 corresponding to C.T. Case No. 02 of  2023 pending in the Court of the learned Designated Court under OPID Act, Cuttack for the alleged commission of offence under Sections 420/467/468/120-B IPC and sec.6 of OPID Act.
 4.
The petitioner was originally remanded in this case on  31.05.2024 as he was in custody in connection with another case.
He was granted interim bail by this Court for a period of 4 weeks  Page 1 of 3  by order dated 15.05.2024, which was subsequently extended till 06.09.2024 .
Since the petitioner surrendered to custody on 09.10.2024.

sentences.text:
Mr. Kar, learned Senior counsel, referring to the affidavit filed by the brother of the petitioner,
who incidentally is the co- accused, submits that the petitioner is ready with demand drafts amounting to Rs. 15 lakhs in all drawn in favour of the 3 informants.
It is further stated in the affidavit that the petitioner is willing to deposit the remaining amount of Rs. 35, 50,000/- to the informants by end of April, 2025.

Mr. Kar submits that in similar cases the petitioner has been granted bail on depositing some portion of the disputed amount, but because no such order has been passed in this case, he continues to be in custody.
6.
Mr. B.Bhuyan, learned State counsel submits that the total amount involved in this case is more than Rs. 13 crores.
Further, the petitioner appears to be a habitual offender, as he is involved in 11 cases of similar nature.
He further submits that the amount purposed to be paid by the petitioner presently is very small compared to the total amount involved.
7. Mr. Pattnaik, learned counsel appearing for one of the informants also opposed the prayer for bail on similar grounds as the State counsel.
8. Considering the submissions made by the parties and on consideration of fact that the petitioner has shown his bonafides by being ready with demand drafts amounting to Rs. 15,00,000/-
, this Court is inclined to take a lenient view, notwithstanding the dispute relating to the total amount allegedly involved.
This is being said for the reason that detaining the petitioner in custody indefinitely shall not enure to the benefit of anyone.
On the contrary, if the petitioner is released, he would be in a better position to abide by his undertaking submitted before this Court.
9. For the foregoing reasons therefore, the bail application is allowed.

Let the petitioner be released on bail on such terms and conditions as the Court below may deem fit and proper to impose including the following conditions:
(i) The petitioner shall submit the demand drafts payable in all amounting in Rs.
15,00,000/- drawn in favour of the informants in the Court below before his release.

(ii) The petitioner shall make all endeavor to repay the remaining amounts, as stated by him under paragraph 5 of the aforementioned affidavit by end of April, 2025,
failing which it shall be open to the prosecution as well as the informants to seek cancellation of bail.
10. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted in course of the day.
